subject: Headroom budgeting + circuit-breaker math for private GPU slab
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Headroom budgeting + circuit-breaker math for private GPU slab

Team / ACME,

Following up from the call this morning — I put together a conservative capacity budget and a simple circuit-breaker model for the private GPU slab we plan to commission for Acme Robotics. Goal: guarantee 95th/99th latency SLOs for the primary workload while absorbing 3x short spikes and keeping egress within their 10 Gbps cap.

Key assumptions (see attached spreadsheet 'slab_headroom_model_v2.xlsx' for the calc):
- Baseline per-request tokens: 250 tokens (avg) -> 1.2k tokens per session including context reuse
- Model: optimized LLM v1 (quantized) -> ~0.9ms/token on our p4-like hardware under sustained batch
- Target throughput: steady 800 qps, burst up to 2,400 qps for 90s windows
- Target latencies: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms

Derived sizing (conservative):
- Sustained slab: 16 GPUs (balanced across 4 racks) -> supports ~900 steady qps with 20% CPU/network headroom
- Burst buffer (warm pool): +8 pre-warmed GPUs for up to 2,400 qps absorption for short windows; warm pool maintained at a 3-min warmup TTL
- Admission control/circuit-breaker thresholds:
  - Soft throttle at 1,200 qps (shed non-critical routes, favor premium tenants)
  - Hard reject at 2,500 qps (protect KV cache / avoid cascade failures)

Egress math (diagram attached 'egress_throttle_diagram.svg'):
- Average token egress per qps: ~1.2k tokens/sec -> ~1.2MB/s per 100 qps (encoded) -> at 2,400 qps ~= 28.8MB/s (~230Mbps) -- this is per-application stream; multi-tenant aggregate planned at <= 10Gbps per Acme contract.
- Plan: per-tenant egress caps + global shaping at top-of-rack egress to guarantee isolation.

Operational asks:
1) Laura: sanity-check the rack-level thermal margin and cooling assumptions (we used 25% margin).
2) Vanessa: please flag any contention modes (network or NVLink saturation) we should account for and whether preemptible burst nodes are safe for Acme SLA.
3) David: confirm the admission-controller hook points in the runtime (per-tenant qps counters and 1s rolling windows).
4) Alice / Acme: quick read and highlight any contract egress constraints I missed.

I attached the model and a diagram to make the numbers traceable. If this sizing looks good we can move the numbers into the provisioning template and the purchase requisition.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slab_headroom_model_v2.xlsx, egress_throttle_diagram.svg

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Headroom budgeting + circuit-breaker math for private GPU slab

Thanks Rishi — good, clear rundown. Quick notes after scanning the spreadsheet: 

- Thermal/Power: the 25% margin is reasonable for early provisioning but please add a flagged column for projected power draw under sustained burst (the chassis we scoped can spike another ~8-10kW per rack during warmup). If Acme's DC has per-rack breakers near capacity we should prefer the staged ramp (8 GPUs warm -> +4 -> +4) to avoid tripping breakers.

- Warm-pool TTL: 3-min is fine for predictable loads, but if Acme expects very spiky telemetry-driven bursts (sub-minute) we should add a <90s 'micro-warm' bucket (1-2 GPUs) and an anticipatory preheat hook from their ingestion signal. That avoids overprovisioning warm pool all day.

- SLA language: the soft throttle you propose is good, but rename 'soft throttle' to 'priority-based admission' and capture explicit route IDs for premium vs background. That makes the rollback path cleaner when we test the CB.

- Security/compliance: ensure egress shaping logs are captured in the audit trail we promised (we need per-tenant egress counters at 1s resolution stored for 30 days). David, can you confirm retention?

I'll update the spreadsheet with a power column and a ramp schedule suggestion and re-upload.

Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure Planning
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Headroom budgeting + circuit-breaker math for private GPU slab

Nice work, Rishi. A couple of operational caveats from the serving/runtime side:

- NVLink & PCIe saturation: at ~2,000 concurrent streams we start to see cross-GPU NVLink contention on our benchmarked transformer kernels. Recommendation: prefer rack-local allocation for burst allocation (pre-warm + place in same rack) to limit cross-rack NVLink/egress pressure. Add a rack affinity constraint to the warm-pool allocator.

- Preemptible bursts: acceptable for background workloads but not for premium routes. For Acme's premium SLA, warm pool must be non-preemptible during contractual hours (08:00-20:00 local). Outside that window we can backfill with preemptible capacity to lower cost.

- Circuit-breaker thresholds: suggest we make them proportional to observed tail-latency rather than static qps numbers. Practical approach: implement three-tier CB using rolling 1m and 5m windows
  - Tier 1 (grace): p95 latency > 120ms -> start shedding background routes at 10% increments every 10s
  - Tier 2 (aggressive): p95 > 180ms or p99 > 350ms -> invoke soft+priority admission to drop non-critical requests immediately
  - Tier 3 (protect): sustained 5m violation or direct hard resource alarms -> disable new admissions and fail fast for low-priority tenants

I'll draft a short runbook for the three-tier CB and an allocator change to respect rack affinity.

Vanessa Ortiz
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Headroom budgeting + circuit-breaker math for private GPU slab

Thanks — this is very helpful and granular. A few items from Acme's side before we lock numbers: 

1) Ingress shaping: our telemetry is bursty and originates from 120 sensors. Can you confirm how the preheat hook would receive a signal (we prefer a simple webhook + token to avoid extra agent installs)?

2) Egress cap: our contract has a hard 10Gbps egress limit at the rack. We like the per-tenant caps + global shaping idea; please surface a worst-case multi-tenant number (aggregate) and an emergency fail-open plan if their edge router denies traffic.

3) SLA hours: confirm where warm pool non-preemptible hours map to our local timezone (we are PST).

If you can add these clarifications into the spreadsheet and the runbook, we can approve the sizing and start procurement.

Appreciate the thoroughness.

— Alice Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Robotics

(On our end I forwarded this to the SRE team for a quick sanity check; they may ping for a short sync.)
